title: Converged credential ops and visibility for admin APIs
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Admin-facing API keys and service tokens are currently governed by fragmented conventions across services: inconsistent naming, ad-hoc rotation cadence, weak audit metadata, and limited per-scope visibility. This makes incident response slower, increases the blast radius from leaked credentials, and complicates RBAC v2 rollout where token purpose and scope need to be machine-assertable.

Goal: Deliver a converged credential operations model for admin APIs that provides: canonical naming conventions that encode environment/scope/owner, automated rotation policies and TTL enforcement, rich audit metadata surfaced to the Console and audit logs, and clear emergency revoke flows. The work must integrate with RBAC v2 and SSO/SAML identity signals so tokens can be scoped and rescinded based on user or role changes.

Out of scope: rotation for end-user session tokens or client SDK ephemeral tokens (handled in separate work).
acceptance_criteria: A naming convention doc published and adopted by 90% of admin API owners (pattern: <team>-<env>-<purpose>-<short-id>)
Central rotation controller enforces minimum rotation windows and optional automated rotation for service tokens (configurable per-project)
Audit logs include token creation, rotation, revoke events with token_metadata fields (creator, team, scope, env, linked-ssoconnect) and are queryable from Console
Console shows per-token last-rotated, expiry, and a one-click emergency revoke action that triggers immediate invalidation across hosted and Dedicated backplanes
RBAC v2 policies can reference token scope labels to grant/deny admin API access; tests demonstrating RBAC policy update + token revoke scenario
Security runbook for emergency revocation validated in tabletop exercise and linked in incident docs
tasks: Design: finalize canonical naming and scope tag schema (drive doc)
Infra: implement token metadata store schema and migration for existing admin keys
Runtime: implement token check-and-reject hook in gateway that consults revocation cache
Orchestration: build central rotation service with policies and scheduled jobs
Console: expose token metadata, rotation controls, and emergency revoke UI
Audit: augment audit log producer to emit structured token events and update ELK mappings
Integrations: wire SSO/SAML identity signals into token ownership claims and automatic suspension on user deprovision
Tests: end-to-end test covering token creation, rotation, revoke, and RBAC policy enforcement
Docs + Migration: migration guide for teams to rename and attach scope labels to existing keys
